I've been farming this same land in Quzhou for over 40 years. My father farmed it before me. I know this soil — it's the sandy loam of the North China Plain, decent for wheat and maize, gets dry in spring and early summer, then floods us in July and August if we're unlucky.

I have 8 mu of contracted land. I'm 60 now, my knees hurt, my son works in Handan city, so I'm doing this mostly alone with my wife helping at busy times. I can't manage cotton — too much hand labor. Vegetables are too much work for the market, though we keep a small kitchen garden.

What I'll do is the same thing I've done for 30 years: **winter wheat followed by summer maize**. The two crops use the same 8 mu in rotation. This is what everyone around here does, the grain station buys it, the input costs are predictable, and I know exactly what to do.

For wheat, I'll use the **Jimai 22** variety — the seed station in town sells it, it's disease-resistant and yields well here. I'll plough and rotary till before planting in October. I put base fertilizer down before seeding: diammonium phosphate plus urea. Then in April I'll top-dress urea at jointing. I irrigate four times: before winter, at jointing, heading, and grain fill. Spring rust has been bad the last few years, so I'll spray once for that, and once more for aphids in May.

For maize after wheat harvest in June, I direct-seed no-till into the stubble — saves time and my back. I use **Zhengdan 958** hybrid seed, same as always. I apply compound fertilizer at planting and top-dress urea when it's knee-high. I'll irrigate if the tasseling period is dry — usually once or twice. Herbicide right after seeding, and I watch for fall armyworm now, that's been getting worse.
